notes: §1985:XIII.3.6.2 prints the clause as `CODE literal-1` (rendered PDF p596 confirms: no IS, no identifier alternative), so at --std 85 the compiler must accept CODE followed by one literal and refuse every other shape. The grammar reportCodeClause is the 2023 `CODE IS? (literal | dataReference)` and nothing gates the 2023-only parts at 85: BindCodeClause screens literal-1's class (COBOL2713) and BindReportDescriptionClauses the at-most-once (COBOL2423), at every edition, and VersionConformancePass has no CODE arm. The witness (CODE "AB") passes and the literal arm is correct. Probes at --std 85: (b) CODE "AB" runs, file starts ABHELLO; CODE IS "AB" exit 0 (should refuse); CODE WS-C (an identifier) exit 0 (should refuse); CODE 12 COBOL2713; CODE "AB" CODE "CD" COBOL2423; CODE with no operand COBOL0001; (d) CODE SPACES and CODE ALL "A" COBOL2713 (a figurative is not a nonnumeric literal, correct); (a) (e) (f) do not reach a one-literal RD clause. (c) is where it fails: the two 2023 additions compile at 85. kb/Work PB5242 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-pipe/slice-50.json).

next.reason: 1985: "CODE literal-1"; 2023: "CODE IS ┤ literal-1 / identifier-1 ├". 2023 format adds an identifier-1 alternative and an optional IS. Programs with CODE identifier are now accepted, which the 1985 literal-only format refused.
